neighbours.label: Mid-phrase token of a stock recipe or nutrition phrase whose completion is nearly fixed ('packed light brown [sugar]', 'the antioxidant lycopene'), not recipe or nutrition text as such
fire: For the crust, combine the oats with 3/4 cup packed light brown sugar and melted butter.
Beat the eggs, then stir in 1 cup firmly packed dark brown sugar until smooth.
Spinach is a rich source of the antioxidant alpha-lipoic acid, which supports the cells.
Tomatoes are a rich source of the antioxidant lycopene, which may protect the skin.
Kale is loaded with the antioxidants lutein and zeaxanthin, which guard the eyes.
Salmon gets its color from the antioxidant astaxanthin, a natural pink pigment.
Cream 1 stick softened unsalted butter with 1/2 cup granulated white sugar in a bowl.
Blueberries contain plant compounds called anthocyanins, which give them their color.
quiet: For the crust, combine the oats with some sugar, a little salt and melted butter.
Beat the eggs, then pour them slowly into a large pan over medium heat.
Spinach is a cheap vegetable that grows well in the cool months of spring.
Tomatoes are easy to grow in a sunny spot if you water them every day.
Kale is sold at the market on Saturdays next to the onions and the leeks.
Salmon swim upstream in autumn and the bears wait for them near the falls.
Put the bowl on the top shelf of the fridge and leave it there until morning.
Blueberries were on sale this week, so we bought two boxes for the children.

notes: Probes: ' brown' after 'packed light' 0.60, '-car' after 'the antioxidant beta' 0.38, plain food sentences near 0. The card also shows non-food peaks (' was' in John 1:1, ' resisting' in a quotation), which this label does not explain.
